close_reason: Fixed when MalformedAnchor was promoted to a struct variant under PKIX-tit4.3. The variant rustdoc now states 'iterator passed to from_der_iter' and does not mention from_pem. The factually-wrong claim is gone.
description:
pkix-truststore/src/lib.rs:232-236 documents Error::MalformedAnchor as:

  /// One certificate in a multi-cert input was malformed. The wrapped
  /// `usize` is the 0-based position of the offending entry in the input
  /// stream (PEM block index for [`from_pem`], iterator index for
  /// [`from_der_iter`]).
  MalformedAnchor(usize),

The 'PEM block index for from_pem' claim is factually wrong. from_pem
(lib.rs:314-335) never returns MalformedAnchor. Its error paths are:

  1. Error::NoCertificates — empty input or no BEGIN boundary.
  2. Error::Pem(DerError) — via map_pem_chain_error when der::ErrorKind::Pem(_).
  3. Error::Der(DerError) — via map_pem_chain_error for any other der::ErrorKind.

map_pem_chain_error at lib.rs:422-428 has no branch that produces
MalformedAnchor. Confirmed by searching: only from_der_iter at lib.rs:378
constructs Error::MalformedAnchor(i).

What goes wrong for a caller in production:

  - A caller writing exhaustive `match err { ... }` over the Error variants
    will be misled into preparing a MalformedAnchor branch for from_pem
    callers — code that will never execute. Wasted code, false sense of
    coverage.
  - A caller writing diagnostic output ('on PEM block %d, ...') will write
    code keyed off MalformedAnchor that the from_pem path never reaches.
    The real PEM-block-index information is hidden inside DerError's
    position field, which is not surfaced through the public API.
  - A reader auditing the public API surface for stability inferences will
    treat the doc as a contract: 'from_pem may produce MalformedAnchor in
    future versions.' That is not the current design intent.

Fix options:

  a) Correct the doc to reference only from_der_iter:
       /// The wrapped `usize` is the 0-based iterator index of the
       /// offending entry. Returned only by [`from_der_iter`].

  b) Make the claim true by routing from_pem failures through MalformedAnchor
     with the PEM block index. This requires either reworking
     map_pem_chain_error to extract the block index from der::Error::position
     (currently discarded), or moving away from x509-cert::load_pem_chain
     to a hand-written multi-block parser that tracks block boundaries.

Option (a) is the cheap fix; option (b) is the principled fix but is a
bigger change that intersects PKIX-tit4.3 (surface der::Error context) and
PKIX-tit4.2 (NoCertificates masks real input errors).
title: Error::MalformedAnchor doc references from_pem but only from_der_iter produces it
